kyoto_isshisoden_nakamura.notes: [Kaiseki · Oike, two hundred years of Kyoto ryori] Behind a white noren on Tomikoji-dori, a house that began in 1827 when the first master carried Wakasa fish along the 鯖街道 (the mackerel road) to the palace and court nobles. Sixth-generation 中村元計 (Motokazu Nakamura) — once a Zen trainee at 天龍寺 and now a doctor of food science — keeps the two dishes passed from father to son: sake-grilled guji, finished as a soup with hot water over the bones, and a white-miso zoni made without dashi. Courses are served in quiet private rooms over a courtyard; reviewers note three Michelin stars. Lunch around ¥20,000–30,000, dinner ¥40,000–50,000; book ahead; closed Sundays.

roles: Sixth-generation master (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: founded in Bunsei 10 (1827) when the first master, 若狭屋清兵衛, carried Wakasa fish such as guji and mackerel to Kyoto for the palace and court nobles; the second generation began catering; the third, a tea devotee, made tea kaiseki catering the core; the fourth supplied the inns 柊家, 俵屋 and 炭家 during the war; after the war the restaurant opened on its present site, and the fifth generation built today's base. The sixth, 中村元計, studied at Tokyo University of Fisheries, trained as a Zen monk at 天龍寺 in 嵯峨嵐山, and in 2021 earned a doctorate in food and agricultural science at 龍谷大学, approaching cooking as science. Tabelog Award Bronze 2017–2023; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021. 2026 reviews call it Michelin three-starred.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「即味心也」 — taste is the heart: only a person's heart moves another's (official site).

Reservation only, by phone 075-525-0009 or the official site (Tabelog; official site). Courses from about ¥50,000 before tax (December 2025) to ¥75,900 (April 2026), plus 15% service (Tabelog). Counter, private tatami rooms and sunken seating (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards (Tabelog). 5 min from Gion-Shijo Stn (Tabelog). Opened 15 January 1988 (Tabelog).
kyoto_gion_maruyama.notes: [Kaiseki · Gion, a quiet room over a rain-washed garden] A Gion kaiseki house since 1988, where private tatami rooms shut out the city and the only sound may be rain in the garden. The cooking is gentle and seasonal rather than showy — in spring, sakura sea bream, firefly squid with broad beans, bamboo shoots in several forms, grilled moroko and a pea-and-egg rice — and beautifully plated. An April 2026 diner notes two Michelin stars. Courses run about ¥50,000–76,000 plus 15% service; book ahead; closed Wednesdays.

roles: Kaiseki house; no person is named in the sources read
chef_bio.background: Per 2025–2026 reviews: a renowned Gion kaiseki restaurant using seasonal ingredients with meticulous presentation; an April 2026 review notes two Michelin stars. Tabelog: opened 15 January 1988; The Tabelog Award Bronze 2018–2021; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021.

kyoto_nijojo_furuta.hours_raw: Lunch 12:00–14:30; dinner from 17:00 with last entry 20:30; closed irregularly (Tabelog). No dinner closing time is published, so no hours are stored. Reservation only, by phone (075-254-8377) or online via the shop's Instagram or Facebook (Tabelog). Omakase from ¥20,000; a course built around chosen ingredients from ¥30,000 at market price (Tabelog); a June 2026 diner paid ¥24,200 including tax for the simplest course; service 10% (Tabelog). kyoto_nijojo_furuta.notes: [Kaiseki · Nijo Castle, a six-seat charcoal counter] Behind a modest sign near Nijo Castle, a counter of six where the owner-chef — trained at Yukimura, Wakuden and Gion Okada, per a November 2025 review — cooks alone over charcoal, letting the fish take its time. Dishes lean on dashi and the grill, and the meal ends with a takikomi rice diners remember. It can feel like being invited into someone's home. Omakase from ¥20,000 plus 10% service; one June 2026 diner found the drinks pricey. Book by phone or via Instagram.

roles: Owner-chef cooking alone (November 2025 reviews); not named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Per November 2025 reviews: the owner-chef trained at Yukimura and worked at Wakuden and Gion Okada, and runs the kitchen single-handed with charcoal cooking. Tabelog: opened 27 April 2016; The Tabelog Award Bronze 2018–2023; Japanese cuisine WEST "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2023.

anecdotes.text: "The charcoal fire never rushed. It patiently waited for the moment when the fish would be at its most delicious." — November 2025.
"The chef managed everything by himself and was incredibly efficient; every dish was outstanding." — November 2025.

kyoto_smart_coffee.vegan_detail: Ask. Black coffee suits; the pancakes, French toast, pudding and sandwiches use eggs, butter or dairy (2026 reviews).
kyoto_smart_coffee.hours_raw: 8:00–19:00 every day (Tabelog); the upstairs western-style lunch room keeps its own hours and is sometimes closed (October 2026). No reservations (Tabelog); weekend and morning queues, shorter on weekday afternoons (October 2026). 38 seats at tables (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Cards: AMEX only (Tabelog). Coffee beans to take away (October 2026). On Teramachi-dori north of Sanjo, 2 min from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_smart_coffee.notes: [Kissaten · Teramachi, Kyoto's pancake kissaten since 1932] A wood-panelled, high-ceilinged coffee house in the Teramachi arcade, said to date from 1932, where the queue forms for the pancakes — crisp outside, soft inside, with butter and maple syrup — and the French toast. The mixed sandwich and the firm, caramel-topped pudding are just as loved, and the coffee is rich and balanced; beans are sold to take home. Upstairs, a western-style lunch room keeps shorter hours. Pancake set ¥1,400; weekday afternoons have the shortest waits. Open daily 8:00–19:00; AMEX only.

roles: Long-established kissaten; no person is named in the sources
chef_bio.background: Per October 2026 reviews: established in 1932 and said to be the second-oldest coffee shop in Kyoto; the first floor is a café and the second a lunch room with its own kitchen. Tabelog Kissaten "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2026.

"It’s rare to be moved by a sandwich, but this one truly impressed me." — October 2026.

kyoto_warder_bakery.notes: [Bakery · Fuyacho, the busy little bread shop] A small bakery by a little park on Fuyacho-dori, its wooden shelves crowded with handwritten labels and more bread arriving from the oven all morning: a Kyoto dashi bread that tastes of iriko and bonito (two per customer), a baked curry bread with curry from Osaka's Navin, Shiba-zuke French, squid-ink bread, and autumn chestnut pies and danishes. Prices are modest, from about ¥270. Takeaway only; cards and IC accepted; closed Wednesday and Thursday.

kyoto_kissa_madrague.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: the menu is toast, sandwiches, spaghetti and curry; the famous egg sandwich comes on thick bread with demi-glace and mustard (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kissa_madrague.vegan_detail: Ask. Food centres on eggs, ham, meat sauce and cheese, and the omelette is made with dashi; juices, tea and black coffee suit (official menu; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_kissa_madrague.hours_raw: 8:00–18:00 every day; last food order 17:00, drinks 17:30; closes early when food runs out; closed irregularly, with notices on Facebook (official site). Seats can be booked at the shop or by phone for 8:00 or 9:30 (morning) or 12:00 (lunch) (official site); lunch seats rotate hourly and walk-ins are possible, but booking is safer (Tabelog). Breakfast until 11:00 (October 2026). Only the Corona sandwich is sold to take away, ordered by phone two days ahead (official site). 18 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Cash only (Tabelog). 9 min walk from Karasuma Oike Stn (official site).
kyoto_kissa_madrague.notes: [Kissaten · Karasuma Oike, the Corona egg sandwich] A retro coffee house in a building that was Kissa Seven for about 50 years from 1963; after its master died in 2011, the son looked for someone to keep the shop going, and Madrague opened that September. About a year later the free paper 音読 asked the shop to carry on the famous egg sandwich of Corona, a western-style restaurant that had just closed, and Corona's master came to teach it in person. The result is a fist-sized, hot, dashi-soft omelette on bread with demi-glace and mustard (¥1,180) — cut it in half to eat. Breakfast sets until 11:00; book a seat for 8:00, 9:30 or 12:00. Open daily 8:00–18:00 (irregular closures); cash only.

roles: Owner (unnamed on the official site), who opened the shop with the owner’s wife
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: before opening, the owner managed a café tied to the revival of Kyoto townhouses and old shopping streets and wanted to get back to hands-on work; while looking for a property with the owner’s wife, the couple met the son of the master of Kissa Seven (in business from 1963 for about 50 years; the master died in 2011) and opened Kissa Madrague there in September 2011. The name is that of Brigitte Bardot’s villa in Saint-Tropez; the owner’s wife loved the actress. The owner once worked part-time at Francois, near Corona, and often ate Corona’s egg sandwich on breaks. The site also describes a team, 京都喫茶文化遺産, formed to take over and keep old neighbourhood kissaten. Tabelog Kissaten "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022, 2026.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site: to keep "the long-running neighbourhood kissaten with tradition", not a retro-styled café, and hand it on to the next generation.
chef_bio.specialty: Corona egg sandwich; Set A breakfast.

anecdotes.text: Per the official site: after customers said the old Corona sandwich had been softer or bigger, the owner reworked the bread, eggs, seasoning, cooking time and heat, the hand pressure when sandwiching and the cut, keeping the basics.
"The egg sandwich is so big that I couldn’t fit it in my mouth in one bite, so I had to cut it in half with a knife." — October 2026.
"It seems there used to be long lines, but now you can easily make a reservation by phone." — October 2026.

kyoto_mariebelle_honten.gf_detail: Ask. The shop sells chocolates (art ganache, Carré de Chocolat) alongside cookies and sablés; the café adds crepes, cheesecake, quiche and gelato; no ingredient list is published (official site; 2026 reviews).
kyoto_mariebelle_honten.vegan_detail: Ask. Many chocolates and the gelato, crepes and cakes use milk, cream or eggs; a 70% dark chocolate is sold but its ingredients are not published (2026 reviews).
kyoto_mariebelle_honten.hours_raw: Shop 11:00–19:00; Cacao Bar (café) 11:00–19:00, last order 18:00; takeaway 11:00–19:00; closed Tuesday; holiday calendar on the official site (official site). kyoto_mariebelle_honten.notes: [Chocolate & café · Sanjo, New York chocolates in a Kyoto townhouse] The Kyoto main shop of MarieBelle, the chocolatier born in New York's SoHo, reached through a narrow alley off Yanagibaba-dori: an antique-furnished townhouse where the art ganache — each piece printed with an artist's design — comes in the brand's blue boxes, and the Cacao Bar serves hot chocolate, crepes, gelato and cheesecake on sofas. Two ganache pieces ¥1,900; café sweets from about ¥1,430. No café bookings; sign in at the door. 11:00–19:00, closed Tuesday.

roles: Brand of chocolatier Maribel Lieberman (New York); no Kyoto staff are named
chef_bio.background: Per the official site: MarieBelle was born in New York’s SoHo (484 Broome St.); the Japanese company MarieBelle Japan runs the Kyoto honten, MarieBelle the Lounge in Daimaru Shinsaibashi (Osaka) and, from 28 October 2026, マリベル渋谷 in Shibuya Scramble Square; cacao is chosen from producing countries, mainly beans grown with support for farms in Honduras, the homeland of Maribel Lieberman; the designs are all paintings made by artists. The Kyoto honten opened on 24 April 2012 (Tabelog) and marked its 14th anniversary in April 2026 (official site). Tabelog Sweets "Tabelog 100" 2018 and Sweets WEST 2018–2020, 2022.
chef_bio.philosophy: Per the official site (in English): "Life is all about the pleasure and happiness we find in food, art and beauty" — Maribel Lieberman, Chocolatier.

kyoto_akagakiya.gf_detail: Ask. A traditional izakaya: duck with a soy-based sauce, oden in broth (with fish cakes), tempura and sashimi with soy sauce; no gluten information (2026 reviews).
kyoto_akagakiya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: oden in broth, duck, fish and yakitori make up most of the menu (2026 reviews).
kyoto_akagakiya.hours_raw: 17:00–23:00 (last order 22:30), Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday and on Mondays that are public holidays (Tabelog). A queue forms from about 16:30; the owner hangs the noren at 17:00 and the first round is seated in arrival order (October–November 2026). Table seats can be booked, for 17:00 or 19:00 starts; the 11 counter seats are walk-in only (Tabelog; November 2026); same-day booking is hard (September 2026). Two-hour limit (October 2026). Menu without prices; bills around ¥4,000–6,000 a head (2026 reviews). 41 seats (11 counter, 30 on tatami); smoking allowed; cash only (Tabelog). 5 min walk from Sanjo Stn (Tabelog).
kyoto_akagakiya.notes: [Izakaya · Kawabata Nijo, a 1930s tavern by the Kamo River] An old izakaya beside the Kamo River, with lantern light, a counter worn smooth and darkened beams; a reviewer gives its founding as 1934 and the move here as 1949. The line forms from 16:30 and the owner hangs the noren at 17:00. Almost every table orders the duck roast; the shime saba, kumiage yuba and Kyoto-style oden (the octopus takes time — order it early) are the other classics. The menu shows no prices, yet bills run around ¥4,000–6,000. Book a table for 17:00 or 19:00; the 11 counter seats are first come. Cash only; smoking allowed; closed Sunday.

roles: Owner (unnamed in the sources)
chef_bio.background: Per an October 2026 review: founded in 1934 (Showa 9) and moved to the present site in 1949 (Showa 24), once a tavern for students and day labourers; reviews disagree on whether the present owner is the third or fourth generation (October 2026). Tabelog Izakaya "Tabelog 100" 2021, 2022 and Izakaya WEST 2024, 2025.

kyoto_zen_cafe_kagizen.notes: [Wagashi café · Gion, Kagizen's quiet café] The café that the old Gion wagashi house Kagizen Yoshifusa opened in 2012 down a back street opposite its ZENBI museum: dim, modern and calm, with a counter and a sofa. Order kuzumochi (¥1,200), the shop's kuzukiri with black syrup, or the seasonal jo-namagashi — chestnut kinton in autumn — with sencha, or come early for the fruit sandwiches, which can be gone before noon.
